newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bougainville Copper keeps the faith.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bougainville Copper keeps the faith.

text.p: The operator of crisis-torn Papua New Guinea's defunct Bougainville copper mine has said it continues to look at options to restart the mine, but hinted the costs of doing so could be greater than once thought.

Bougainville Copper Ltd, chased off remote Bougainville island eight years ago after its huge Panguna mine became the focus of a secessionist uprising, said in its 1996 annual report that cost estimates of up to 600 million kina (US$434 million) could be dated.
"Past studies have indicated that estimated start-up costs are at the upper end of K400-600 million," chairman David Karpin said in the report.

"As the passage of time increases and with lack of access to the island and the possible deterioration of the equipment, these figures increasingly become uncertain and may not reflect an accurate estimate."
The annual report was lodged with the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday. Bougainville Copper is owned 53.6 percent by global mining giant RTZ-CRA.

Karpin repeated his estimate that the company would need about 18 months to recommission the mine, but said last year's murder of Bougainville premier Theodore Miriung set back further the prospect of a political settlement on the island.

The report was prepared well before this week's unprecedented political crisis in Papua New Guinea, sparked by army resistence to the government's decision to use foreign mercenaries to help quell unrest on Bougainville.
Miriung, a former rebel and strong advocate of a peaceful solution to the Bougainville conflict, was shot dead last October. An official inquiry implicated troops in his murder.
"This has undoubtedly caused further mistrust and set back any hopes there may have been for a peaceful resolution in the near future," Karpin said.
Karpin was not immediately available for comment on Wednesday.
The Panguna deposit's recoverable reserves are 496 million tonnes of ore at an average grade of 0.42 percent copper and 0.55 grams per tonne of gold.
